subject: Using lapply to iterate over a list of aesthetic mappings

messages.author: 15be55a18eb0fb97
messages.subject: Using lapply to iterate over a list of aesthetic mappings
parts:
Hi all, if we take the iris data.frame:
data(iris)

I wish to map Sepal.Length to x, and Sepal.Width to y, and I would like to create three more plots by iterating over the remaining variables in the data.frame for the colour aesthetic. I've tried to do this by creating a list of plots using lapply as shown below, but for some reason, the colours take on a single value for each plot. Could someone please guide me as to where I'm going wrong?

Many thanks
Hefin

library(ggplot2)

plots <- lapply(colnames(iris)[3:5], function(i){
  ggplot(iris, aes(Sepal.Length, Sepal.Width, col = i)) + geom_point()
})

plots

Ah I did not know about aes_string. This is perfect, thank you Ista.

Hefin

On Monday, 15 May 2017 16:08:22 UTC+1, Ista Zahn wrote:
colnames gives you column names as a character vector, so you'll need
something like

plots <- lapply(colnames(iris)[3:5], function(i){
  ggplot(iris, aes_string("Sepal.Length", "Sepal.Width", col = i)) +
geom_point()
})

Best,
Ista
